issue.title: unable to require state interfaces exported by chainable controller
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
I have a `controller_interface::ChainableControllerInterface` that basically processes/fuses IMU data and thus only needs to import and export state interfaces.

Essentially, it is a `controller_interface::ChainableControllerInterface` that requires the state interfaces:
```C++
controller_interface::InterfaceConfiguration state_interface_configuration() const override
  {
    std::vector<std::string> interface_names = {
      //
      sensor_name + "/angular_velocity.x",
      sensor_name + "/angular_velocity.y",
      sensor_name + "/angular_velocity.z",
      //
      sensor_name + "/linear_acceleration.x",
      sensor_name + "/linear_acceleration.y",
      sensor_name + "/linear_acceleration.z",
    };
    if (use_magnetometer)
    {
      interface_names.push_back(sensor_name + "/magnetic_field.x");
      interface_names.push_back(sensor_name + "/magnetic_field.y");
      interface_names.push_back(sensor_name + "/magnetic_field.z");
    }
    return {controller_interface::interface_configuration_type::INDIVIDUAL, interface_names};
  }
```
and exports the state interfaces:
```C++
std::vector<hardware_interface::StateInterface> on_export_state_interfaces() override
  {
    std::vector<hardware_interface::StateInterface> state_interfaces;

    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/angular_velocity.x", &angular_velocity.x()));
    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/angular_velocity.y", &angular_velocity.y()));
    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/angular_velocity.z", &angular_velocity.z()));

    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/linear_acceleration.x", &linear_acceleration.x()));
    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/linear_acceleration.y", &linear_acceleration.y()));
    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/linear_acceleration.z", &linear_acceleration.z()));

    if (use_magnetometer)
    {
      state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
        get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/magnetic_field.x", &magnetic_field->x()));
      state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
        get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/magnetic_field.y", &magnetic_field->y()));
      state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
        get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/magnetic_field.z", &magnetic_field->z()));
    }

    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/orientation.w", &q_wi.w()));
    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/orientation.x", &q_wi.x()));
    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/orientation.y", &q_wi.y()));
    state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(
      get_node()->get_name(), get_name() + "/orientation.z", &q_wi.z()));
    return state_interfaces;
  }
```

This works as expected. `ros2 control list_controllers -v` will show the correct state interfaces:
```
	update_rate: 500 Hz
	is_async: False
	claimed interfaces:
	required command interfaces:
	required state interfaces:
		base_imu/angular_velocity.x
		base_imu/angular_velocity.y
		base_imu/angular_velocity.z
		base_imu/linear_acceleration.x
		base_imu/linear_acceleration.y
		base_imu/linear_acceleration.z
		base_imu/magnetic_field.x
		base_imu/magnetic_field.y
		base_imu/magnetic_field.z
	chained to interfaces:
	exported reference interfaces:
	exported state interfaces:
		fusion/angular_velocity.x
		fusion/angular_velocity.y
		fusion/angular_velocity.z
		fusion/linear_acceleration.x
		fusion/linear_acceleration.y
		fusion/linear_acceleration.z
		fusion/magnetic_field.x
		fusion/magnetic_field.y
		fusion/magnetic_field.z
		fusion/orientation.w
		fusion/orientation.x
		fusion/orientation.y
		fusion/orientation.z
```

However, using this with an `imu_sensor_broadcaster/IMUSensorBroadcaster` and `sensor_name: fusion` fails with:
```
Unable to activate controller 'fusion_sensor_broadcaster' since the state interface 'fusion/orientation.x' is not available.
```
although it is clearly visible that the `required state interfaces` strings match the `exported state interfaces` above:
```
fusion_sensor_broadcaster imu_sensor_broadcaster/IMUSensorBroadcaster  inactive
	update_rate: 500 Hz
	is_async: False
	claimed interfaces:
	required command interfaces:
	required state interfaces:
		fusion/orientation.x
		fusion/orientation.y
		fusion/orientation.z
		fusion/orientation.w
		fusion/angular_velocity.x
		fusion/angular_velocity.y
		fusion/angular_velocity.z
		fusion/linear_acceleration.x
		fusion/linear_acceleration.y
		fusion/linear_acceleration.z
	chained to interfaces:
	exported reference interfaces:
	exported state interfaces:
```

The same `IMUSensorBroadcaster` works when I specify the namespace of a "real" IMU (`hardware_interface::SensorInterface`).

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. create a `ChainableControllerInterface` with only state interface export/imports
2. try to import the state interfaces from another controller

**Expected behavior**
A controller should be able to require state interfaces of another chainable controller.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: Ubuntu
 - Version jazzy

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here, especially include any modifications to ros2_control that relate to this issue.

comments.body:
Hello!

The sensor name needs to be the name of the exporting controller + /fusion. Then it should find it. 

All exported interfaces are prepended with the name of their exporting controller.

comments.body:
> All exported interfaces are prepended with the name of their exporting controller.

You are right. If I export the state interfaces of a controller that I configure with name `fusion` like:
```C++
state_interfaces.emplace_back(hardware_interface::StateInterface(get_name(), "angular_velocity.x", &angular_velocity.x()));
```
and configure the `IMUSensorBroadcaster` with `sensor_name: fusion`, it indeed does not complain anymore. 

But this is somehow not visible in the `exported state interfaces`. I.e., whatever prefix I chose for `StateInterface`, it does not show in the name of the exported state. Now, the overview looks like:
```
fusion                    uav/fusion/FusionMadgwick                    active
	required state interfaces:
		base_imu/angular_velocity.x

fusion_sensor_broadcaster imu_sensor_broadcaster/IMUSensorBroadcaster  active
	required state interfaces:
		fusion/angular_velocity.x
````

I guess you just have to know that state interfaces are automatically prefixed with the controller name. I expected this to work like the ROS topics where you would see matching topics. Maybe it would help to show these automatically prefixed state interfaces like the private topics (`~/`).
